title: Why I Started Setting Boundaries at Work
script: Narrator: [tired but honest] For almost two years, I answered work messages at every hour, because I was afraid of seeming lazy or uncommitted to my team.
Narrator: [reflective] I would reply to emails during dinner, during weekends, and sometimes even while I was supposed to be resting on vacation.
Narrator: [honest] Nobody actually forced me to do this. I built that habit myself, slowly, without noticing how exhausted it was making me.
Narrator: [with feeling] The moment I realized something was wrong happened during my sister's birthday dinner, when I answered three messages before the cake was even served.
Narrator: [thoughtful] She didn't say anything cruel, she just looked disappointed, and that expression stayed with me for days afterward.
Narrator: [determined] So I decided to change something small first, turning off work notifications after seven in the evening, unless something was truly urgent.
Narrator: [honest] The first week felt uncomfortable, almost like I was doing something wrong by simply not answering immediately.
Narrator: [surprised] But nothing terrible happened. My manager didn't complain, my coworkers adjusted, and the world kept turning without my instant replies.
Narrator: [warmly] Slowly, I extended this boundary to weekends too, only checking messages once on Saturday morning, instead of constantly throughout both days.
Narrator: [reflective] What surprised me most was how much clearer my thinking became once I wasn't mentally half at work all the time.
Narrator: [thoughtful] I used to believe boundaries meant caring less about my job, although now I understand it differently.
Narrator: [gently] Boundaries actually let me care more, because I show up focused and rested, instead of tired and quietly resentful.
Narrator: [honest] My sister noticed the change first, actually. She said I finally seemed present during our conversations, not just physically there.
Narrator: [warmly] That comment meant more to me than any compliment I ever received about my work performance.
Narrator: [encouraging] If you're constantly available for everyone else, consider starting small too, maybe just one quiet hour that belongs completely to you.
